# The 7 ms audit — frozen contract

**Owned by the lead. Do not edit this file.** Every lane implements against it.

## What this audit is answering

The operator asked whether the tool is *truly* as responsive as the terminal,
across **every clickable control**. The benchmark is not a preference — it was
measured on 2026-09-04:

| | |
|---|---|
| bare console app answers a key | 1.8 ms |
| **real claude TUI answers an arrow key** | **6.9 ms — THE BAR** |
| one screen read, held-open reader | 9.3 ms |
| one screen read, spawned child | 99.8 ms |

**The bar is 7.0 ms.** The operator chose it explicitly over a one-frame (16 ms)
budget: match the terminal exactly.

🔴 **The existing perf gate is calibrated to 50 ms** — `GESTURE` and `INSTANT`
are both `50.0` in `tests/perf-driver.ps1`. Everything in the tool can be **7×
slower than the terminal** and that suite still reports green. Its "everything
is inside its class budget" is therefore not evidence of anything this audit is
asking. Do not quote it as such.

🔴 **And its coverage check is blind to a third of the surface.** The regex at
`tests/perf-driver.ps1:610` counts only
`Click|SelectionChanged|TextChanged|KeyDown|Checked|MouseDoubleClick`. Measured:
**50 distinct `$ui.*` controls carry a handler**, and the kinds the regex never
sees are `MouseLeftButtonUp` (6), `PreviewMouseLeftButtonDown` (3),
`MouseLeftButtonDown` (3), `PreviewKeyDown` (2), `SizeChanged` (2),
`PreviewMouseRightButtonDown` (1), `PreviewMouseLeftButtonUp` (1),
`LostKeyboardFocus` (1) — which is exactly how this UI wires its custom borders.

## 🔴 SAFETY — the one rule that outranks the audit

**The operator has ~31 live claude sessions running that they cannot relaunch.**

**NEVER invoke a handler that launches, kills, types, saves, sends, signs in, or
writes to disk.** Not once, not "just to time it". `RelaunchSessions` kills
sessions. `OpenNotRunning` launches them. `SendBtn`/`CastSend` type into live
consoles. `SaveBtn` writes the registry. `SignIn` opens a terminal.

Measure those the way `perf-driver.ps1` already does — **time the work the
handler does BEFORE the irreversible step** (`Get-TickedPlan`, `Get-LaunchBlock`,
`Build-Cast`, `Get-SRRegistryStamp`, the guard and the enable/disable pass) and
record the control as `GUARDED`, naming which function you timed instead.
Anything you change, change back.

If you cannot measure a control without a side effect, the honest verdict is
`UNMEASURABLE` plus the reason. **An unmeasured control reported as fast is the
worst output this audit can produce.**

## Ownership — structural, not by convention

`lib/sessions-window.ps1` is 474 KB and `lib/_common.ps1` is 370 KB; effectively
the whole tool lives in two files. So lanes **cannot** own subsystems by file.

- **You create exactly ONE new file:** `tests/audit-<lane>.ps1`
- **You write exactly ONE report:** `tests/audit/<lane>.md`
- **You edit NOTHING else.** Not `sessions-window.ps1`, not `_common.ps1`, not
  `perf-driver.ps1`, not `run-tests.ps1`, not this contract, not another lane's
  files. The lead applies every fix.
- **Run no git commands at all.** Shared working tree; the lead commits.

## How to measure

Your driver is spliced onto the built window by the harness in
`tests/run-tests.ps1` — copy how `perf-driver.ps1` is invoked:

```powershell
$h = New-GuiHarness -Driver 'audit-<lane>.ps1' -OutFile 'audit-<lane>-test.ps1' -Gui 'sessions-window.ps1'
& powershell.exe -STA -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $h -NoScan
```

🪤 **The driver is APPENDED into the window's own scope.** Any top-level
`$x = ...` writes the same scope the GUI keeps state in, and the harness will
**throw** if you assign a name the GUI uses as `$script:` state (`$live`,
`$rows`, `$said`, `$model`, …). Prefix your locals — `$aFoo` — and the guard
stays quiet.

**Timing method, identical in every lane:**

- **Best of 15.** The fastest run is the only sample that got the CPU it asked
  for; everything above it is contention. Report best, median and p90.
- Wrap in `[Diagnostics.Stopwatch]`, `| Out-Null` the result.
- 🔴 **An operation that threw has no timing, it has an error.** Catch, and
  record it as `THREW` with the message — never as a number. A benchmark that
  reports the cost of throwing is worse than no benchmark.
- Record the machine: run a fixed CPU loop (100k `[Math]::Sqrt`) once and report
  it, plus the count of running `claude` processes. A table that moved because
  the machine did must be readable as such.

## Verdicts — use exactly these

| verdict | meaning |
|---|---|
| `AT BAR` | best ≤ 7.0 ms |
| `NEAR` | best ≤ 16 ms (inside one 60 fps frame, but over the bar) |
| `OVER` | best > 16 ms — say what dominates |
| `GUARDED` | destructive; the pre-step was timed instead. Name the function. |
| `UNMEASURABLE` | could not be timed without a side effect. Say why. |

## The report — `tests/audit/<lane>.md`

Lead with a one-line count (`n AT BAR, n NEAR, n OVER, n GUARDED, n UNMEASURABLE`),
then one row per control:

```
| control | handler | what pressing it does | best | med | p90 | verdict | what dominates |
```

Then, and this is the part the lead most needs:

1. **The worst three, diagnosed** — not just "slow", but *which call* inside the
   handler owns the time. Time the parts.
2. **Anything the handler does that a click should not be paying for** — disk,
   a subprocess, a screen read, a full rebuild where an append would do.
3. **Any control you found that the coverage map does not name at all.**
4. **What you could not measure, and what would make it measurable.**

Write what you measured, not what you expect. A lane reporting everything green
is a lane the lead has to re-run.
